title: 1 + 2 + … + 100 in seconds? Young Gauss's famous trick
description:
Brunswick, around 1786: nine-year-old Carl Friedrich Gauss solves a long addition problem while the rest of the class is still adding. Here's how the famous pairing trick works – and why the oldest source never mentions 1 to 100.

One true story from the history of math – every day.
Created with AI assistance (animation and voice); facts from the sources listed.

Sources:
· W. Sartorius von Waltershausen, Gauss zum Gedächtniss (1856)
· F. A. T. Winnecke, Gauss – ein Umriss seines Lebens und Wirkens (1877)
· Brian Hayes, Gauss's Day of Reckoning, American Scientist 94 (2006)
· MacTutor History of Mathematics, Johann Carl Friedrich Gauss (St Andrews)
